Meta.title: Sahih Explorer · Chains of narration of the six hadith collections
Meta.description: Follow any hadith of the six canonical collections through its chain of narrators to the Prophet ﷺ, see where chains meet, and read what each narrator's record says.

Footer.title: Sahih Explorer
Footer.tagline: Making the science of hadith transmission visible: every chain, every narrator, every link.
Footer.disclaimer: A study aid built from open data. Gradings shown are those published by the scholars named; automatic notes are observations, not rulings. Verify with qualified scholars.

Search.title: Search
Search.placeholder: A reference (bukhari 1), words from a hadith, or a narrator's name
Search.noResults: Nothing found. Try fewer words, another spelling, or the Arabic.
Search.tips: Type a reference such as “muslim 1907a” to go straight to it. Arabic search ignores vowel marks and spelling variants of alif, ya and ta marbuta.

Graph.gap: Someone is missing here: the text names a narrator the dataset does not identify, or the report reaches the Prophet ﷺ without a Companion.

Hadith.noStandardRef: Not matched to a standard edition; number {n} in the source dataset
Hadith.gradingsSource: Published gradings as collected in the public-domain Hadith API, attributed to each scholar. Scholars sometimes differ; see the glossary for the terms.
Hadith.sahihainNote: Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim are accepted by the scholars of hadith as authentic collections, so individual gradings are not listed for them.
Hadith.noGradings: No published grading has been matched to this hadith yet.
Hadith.textHelp: Underlined names link to each narrator. A dashed underline marks a narrator added from the text where the dataset's chain stopped short.
Hadith.translationApi: English translation from the public-domain Hadith API, matched to this Arabic text.
Hadith.translationDataset: English translation from the source dataset.
Hadith.noTranslation: No English translation is available for this hadith yet.
Hadith.chainHelp: From the Prophet ﷺ at the top to the compiler at the bottom. Colours show each narrator's recorded reliability; the Arabic word on each link is how the narrator received it.
Hadith.chainList: Narrators in order, with how each received the report
Hadith.noChain: The dataset links no narrators to this hadith.
Hadith.relatedHelp: Reports in the six collections whose wording closely matches this one, and their chains drawn together.
Hadith.mergedHelp: Thicker links carry more chains. Narrators of this hadith's own chain are drawn strongest.

Notes.disclaimer: Automatic observations from the dataset to help you study this chain: what it records about each narrator and link. They are not a grading of the hadith.
Notes.none: Nothing in the dataset calls for comment on this chain.
Notes.noGrade: {name} has no reliability grade in the dataset.
Notes.unidentified: One narrator in this chain (ID {id}) is missing from the narrator records.
Notes.genGap: {student} (generation {studentGen}) is recorded as narrating from {teacher} (generation {teacherGen}). A direct link across that many generations is unusual; one of the two may be misidentified.
Notes.genOrder: {student} is placed in generation {studentGen}, well before their teacher {teacher} (generation {teacherGen}). Check the identification.
Notes.deathGap: {student} died in {studentDeath} AH, {years} years after {teacher} ({teacherDeath} AH). Direct hearing across that span is hard to reconcile.
Notes.deathOrder: {student} died in {studentDeath} AH, long before {teacher} ({teacherDeath} AH).
Notes.unattested: The link from {teacher} to {student} appears nowhere else in the dataset.
Notes.hidden: Between {teacher} and {student} the text also names {names}, who is not identified in the dataset.
Notes.nameDiffers: The text names “{text}”, which matches {alt}; the dataset links {name}. Scholars tell such narrators apart by era, teachers and students.
Notes.inferred: {names}: not in the dataset's chain; added because the text names them next and they are a known teacher of the narrator before them.
Notes.noChain: The dataset links no narrators to this hadith.
Notes.branched: The text switches between chains (ح). The graph shows each chain and where they meet.
Notes.uncertainBranch: The text switches between chains (ح), and at least one meeting point was inferred rather than read from the text.
Notes.notMarfu: The text does not mention the Prophet ﷺ after the chain, so it is drawn ending with {name}: it may be that narrator's own statement or description.
Notes.sourceNotCompanion: The chain as listed ends with {name}, who is not a Companion, yet the text reaches the Prophet ﷺ. Either a narrator is missing from the dataset here, or the report is mursal (a Successor citing the Prophet ﷺ directly).
Notes.followUp: This entry gives another chain for the report before it (“the same”, “similar”) rather than a full text.

Narrator.metaDescription: {name}: {grade}. Teachers, students and the {count} hadith records whose chains include this narrator in the six collections.
Narrator.verdictHelp: The Arabic wording recorded in the source, in the terminology of Ibn Hajar's Taqrib al-Tahdhib, with its symbols for the books the narrator appears in.
Narrator.sameNameHelp: {count, plural, one {# other narrator shares} other {# other narrators share}} this first name and father's name. Chains often cite narrators this briefly, so scholars tell them apart by era, teachers and students.
Narrator.companionsWhoNarrate: Companions who narrate from him ﷺ
Narrator.networkHelp: Teachers above, students below, the most frequent links first. Line width shows how many chains in the six collections use the link.
Narrator.linksHelp: Links come from the source's teacher and student lists and from the chains themselves, so each appears on both people's pages. “Listed only” means no chain in the six collections uses it.
Narrator.termsHelp: The transmission word on the links into this narrator.
Narrator.mapHelp: Positions are approximate; regions are shown as circles.
Narrator.prophetHadiths: {count} hadith records in this dataset have a chain reaching the Prophet ﷺ.
Narrator.noHadiths: No hadith in the six collections include this narrator in their chains.
Narrator.wikiPrompt: Look for this narrator on Wikipedia. Many narrators share names, so a result is shown only if it mentions their death year.
Narrator.wikiAutomatic: Automatic match: check it is the same person

Collections.title: The six collections
Collections.description: The six canonical Sunni collections (al-Kutub al-Sitta), book by book, with every chain drawn and linked.
Collections.gradesNote: Published gradings are shown for Sunan Abi Dawud, Jami' al-Tirmidhi, Sunan an-Nasa'i and Sunan Ibn Majah. The two Sahihs are accepted as authentic by the scholars of hadith, so individual gradings are not listed for them.
Collections.collectionDescription: {name}, book by book, with the chain of narration of every hadith.
Collections.summary: {hadiths} hadith in {books} books · {graded} with published gradings · {english} with English translation
Collections.summarySahih: {hadiths} hadith in {books} books · accepted as authentic by the scholars of hadith · {english} with English translation

Connect.title: Did A narrate from B?
Connect.description: Check whether the records link a student to a teacher, how many chains use the link, and how else knowledge could have passed between them.
Connect.typeName: Type a name in English or Arabic

verdict.direct: Yes: {student} narrates from {teacher} in {count, plural, one {# chain} other {# chains}} of the six collections.
verdict.listed: The source lists {teacher} among the teachers of {student}, but no chain in the six collections uses the link.
verdict.indirect: No direct link is recorded, but chains connect {teacher} to {student} through other narrators.
verdict.reverse: The records show the opposite: {teacher} narrates from {student}.
verdict.none: The records connect {teacher} to {student} neither directly nor through up to six narrators.

Connect.alsoListed: The source's teacher and student lists record it too.
Connect.datesFar: Their recorded death years are {years} years apart, which makes a direct meeting unlikely.
Connect.datesConsistent: Their recorded generations and death years are consistent with a direct meeting.
Connect.datesOpen: Their recorded dates alone do not settle whether they met.
Connect.pathsHelp: Each step is a teacher-to-student link recorded in the source or used in a chain.
Connect.caveat: This reflects the dataset only. Whether a narrator actually heard from a teacher is established by the scholars' books of narrators (rijal) and of hidden defects ('ilal).

Glossary.title: Glossary
Glossary.description: The terms used across the site: narrator grades, generations, words of transmission, published gradings, and how the chain notes are made.
Glossary.gradesHelp: The reliability label recorded for each narrator. The wording follows Ibn Hajar al-Asqalani's Taqrib al-Tahdhib, whose ranks order the labels here.
Glossary.generationsHelp: Ibn Hajar's twelve generations, used by the source to place each narrator in time.
Glossary.termsHelp: The word before each name in a chain tells how that narrator received the report.
Glossary.gradingsHelp: Terms used in the gradings shown on hadith pages.
Glossary.notes: How the chain notes are made
Glossary.notesHelp: Each hadith page lists automatic observations. They restate what the dataset records; they do not grade the hadith.

grade.title: Narrator grade
grade.body: Shown when a narrator's recorded grade is below “truthful” (for example “acceptable”, “unknown”, “weak”), so you can look closer.

no-grade.title: No grade recorded
no-grade.body: The dataset has no reliability label for this narrator; it does not mean they are weak.

unidentified.title: Missing narrator record
unidentified.body: The chain refers to a narrator ID that has no record in the dataset.

unattested.title: Link seen only here
unattested.body: This teacher-to-student link is neither in the source's lists nor in any other chain. Such links deserve a check in the books of narrators.

hidden.title: Unidentified narrator in between
hidden.body: The text names someone between two narrators, but the dataset does not identify them. The graph draws this link dashed.

inferred.title: Narrator added from the text
inferred.body: Where the dataset's chain stops short, the next name in the text is added only if it matches exactly one known teacher of the narrator before it.

nameDiffers.title: Name points elsewhere
nameDiffers.body: A distinctive name in the text (such as a place or tribal name) belongs to a different narrator than the one the dataset linked.

genGap.title: Wide generation gap
genGap.body: Teacher and student are recorded six or more generations apart (routine gaps are one to four).

deathGap.title: Death years far apart
deathGap.body: The student died 120 or more years after the teacher, or 80 or more years before them.

branched.title: Switch between chains (ح)
branched.body: The text gives more than one chain. Branches are joined where the text or the records show they meet.

notMarfu.title: Does not reach the Prophet ﷺ
notMarfu.body: The text after the chain does not mention the Prophet ﷺ; the report may be a Companion's or a later narrator's own words (mawquf or maqtu').

sourceNotCompanion.title: Source is not a Companion
sourceNotCompanion.body: The chain's last listed narrator is not a Companion although the text reaches the Prophet ﷺ: a Companion is missing from the dataset, or the report is mursal.

followUp.title: Additional chain
followUp.body: Entries ending with “the same” or “similar” give another chain for the previous report.

About.title: About
About.intro: Sahih Explorer turns the chain of narration (isnad) of every hadith in the six canonical collections from a list of names into a map you can follow: back to the Prophet ﷺ, across the narrators' lives, and between collections where the same report was preserved.
About.step1: The source dataset records {narrators} narrators, with biographies, grades, teachers and students, and {hadiths} hadith records whose chains list narrator IDs.
About.step2: Each listed chain is matched against the Arabic text of the hadith: {share} of listed narrators are found in the text, together with the word used to receive the report (haddathana, akhbarana, 'an…).
About.step3: The text also shows what a flat list cannot: narrators cited together, switches between chains (ح), names the dataset does not identify, and where the chain stops short. {inferred} narrators were added from the text under strict conditions, and are marked as such.
About.step4: Each hadith is matched by its Arabic text to the public-domain Hadith API: {matched} records gained a standard reference number and {graded} gained published gradings, each credited to the scholar who made it.
About.step5: Reports with closely matching wording are grouped across and within the collections: {groups} groups covering {hadiths} records, so you can see where their chains meet.
About.not: This is a study aid, not a verdict. Gradings are those of the named scholars. The notes on each chain are automatic observations from the data; a hadith's grade is established by scholars who weigh all its chains, narrators and text.
About.sourceDataset: Narrator records and chains: an open dataset of the six collections' narrators and chains (see DATA.md for what is known of its provenance).
About.sourceApi: Standard reference numbers, published gradings and some English translations: the Hadith API by Fawaz Ahmed (public domain),
About.sourceWikipedia: Wikipedia summaries, only when you ask for them on a narrator's page.
About.limitDeaths: Death years are recorded for only {share} of narrators, so date checks are often unavailable.
About.limitGaps: {count} hadith records have a link where the text names a narrator the dataset does not identify; these are drawn as dashed links.
About.limitIdentity: Narrators who share a name can be misidentified by the dataset. Where the text points to another person, the chain notes say so.
About.limitEnglish: {count} hadith records have no English translation yet.
About.limitCoverage: The dataset does not contain every hadith of every edition (for example, some of Sunan Ibn Majah is missing).
About.corrections: Every hadith and narrator page has a “Report an error” link that opens a pre-filled issue. Corrections to the data go into the source files and pass the same integrity checks as everything else.
About.license: The code is MIT licensed. The data can be downloaded and used through the API; see the developer page for the terms of each source.

Developers.title: Developers
Developers.intro: Everything on the site is available as JSON: collections, hadith with their chains and notes, narrators with their links, search, and the path finder.
Developers.apiHelp: Read-only, no key needed, CORS enabled, cached for an hour. Please cache on your side too.

endpoint.index: Version, data build and the list of endpoints.
endpoint.book: All hadith of one book, summarised.
endpoint.hadith: One hadith: Arabic and English text, references, gradings, narrator mentions in the text, the chain graph (edges, gaps, inferred narrators), notes and related reports.
endpoint.narrator: One narrator: names, grade, generation, dates, places, family, teachers and students with link counts, statistics.
endpoint.narratorHadiths: The hadith a narrator appears in, ten per page, optionally for one collection.
endpoint.search: Search narrators and hadith. A reference such as “bukhari 1” resolves directly.
endpoint.connect: Whether a student narrates from a teacher, and the shortest chains between them.

Developers.dataset: Each tagged release attaches the built dataset (narrators, hadith, chain edges) as JSON Lines and CSV, with the integrity report.
Developers.build: The data build is deterministic and checked: it fails if any integrity limit is exceeded. Details in
Developers.terms: Code: MIT. Hadith API material: public domain. The source dataset's own terms are described in DATA.md; please credit Sahih Explorer and the original sources when you reuse the data.
